label: digit 0 fed back as input at copy steps L+1/L+2 (echo of original token 0 or 1)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase when the fed-back input token is the digit 0 and the step is one of the first two copy steps (recall_idx 1 or 2), i.e. the model is echoing back original token 0 or original token 1 being "0". Magnitude is strongly set by position: when 0 was the first original token (input at step L+1, recall_idx 1) activations are high (~3.5-4.3, all top quartiles; 80% of mass); when 0 was the second original token (recall_idx 2) activations are weak (~0.8-1.5). Does not fire on 0 in the original phase, on the delimiter, on 0 inputs later in the copy phase (recall_idx >= 3), or on any other token (other digits included). Output token and sequence length have essentially no effect beyond position.

issues: The explanation says sequence length 'has essentially no effect'. That is false for the recall_idx==2 clause. Test split, (phase==2)&(in_tok==0)&(recall_idx==2): at L==3 it is predicted on 450 steps with precision 0.0 (never fires); at L==4 precision is 0.546 (2451 predicted); at L==5 precision is 0.9996. All 1564 test false positives of the original predicate come from this class. In misses they show up as short sequences like 'd 0 a 1 <DEL> d *0*', where 0 is the second original token and L=4, or 'n 0 3 <DEL> n *0*' with L=3.

The core claim holds. All activation is in the copy phase and 100% of mass is on in_tok==0. recall_idx 1 carries 80% of the mass and recall_idx 2 carries 20%. The recall_idx==1 clause alone has test precision 1.0 and mass recall 0.80. Missed activations are 13 tiny scattered steps holding 0.0% of the mass.
The original predicate's test precision of 0.954 comes from the systematic length gap described above, not from scattered noise.
Minor: the label says 'copy steps L+1/L+2', but the recall_idx 2 echo only fires reliably when L>=5, partially when L=4, and never when L=3.
skeptic.revised_label: digit 0 fed back as input at the first copy steps: strong when echoing original token 0 (recall_idx 1); weak when echoing original token 1 (recall_idx 2), but only for longer sequences (never at L=3, about half the time at L=4)
